pages.title: The Realm of Direction
pages.body: Spells are ordered geometric programs. Begin at north on the outer ring, read clockwise, then move inward. A valid program reshapes the world; a broken one fails at the physical sigil that caused the fault.

elements.label: Compiler's field kit
elements.alt: A sigil tome beside a three-ring circle, with the north slot marked in gold.

elements.label: Clockwise, then inward
elements.alt: Numbered sigils travel clockwise around the outer ring before continuing on the next ring.

elements.label: Learn to gather mana
elements.alt: Open the mana source page.

pages.title: Your First Cast
pages.body: Build and draw from a mana source, hold the Firebolt Sigil Tome, aim, and use it. Casting is server-authoritative: the server resolves collision, mana, damage, and the final result.

elements.label: Firebolt checklist
elements.alt: Draw mana, hold the tome, aim at a safe target, and use the item.

elements.label: Ponder a complete cast
elements.alt: Animate compiler order, mana quote, and the actual executed VM ticks.

pages.title: Finite Crystal Sources
pages.body: You begin with zero mana and zero capacity. Craft a source and shards. Constructed sources hold eight finite charges. Buried natural crystals mature and recharge only while loaded and supported by conductive geology; nearby natural sources slow one another.

elements.label: The attuned mana network
elements.alt: A central mana crystal branches to eight elemental source stations, showing mana as a finite routed network.

elements.label: Mana crystal source
elements.alt: A shaped recipe using amethyst blocks, lapis blocks, and crying obsidian.

elements.label: Capacity shard
elements.alt: A shapeless recipe combining amethyst, lapis, and glowstone dust.

elements.label: Attuned remote draw
elements.alt: Mana weakens with inverse-square distance and only crosses a loaded chunk in the same dimension.

elements.label: Build storage and conduits
elements.alt: Open the tiered mana infrastructure page.

pages.title: Storage and Conduits
pages.body: Route one loaded source through a matching conduit tier into persistent storage. Crystal Vials hold 200 μ through Raw Crystal Conduits (8 blocks, 25 μ/tick, 80% efficient). Runed Cells hold 1,000 μ through Runed Conduits (24 blocks, 100 μ/tick, 95%). Resonant Vaults hold 8,000 μ through Resonant Conduits (64 blocks, 400 μ/tick, lossless). Use a store for status; sneak-use to draw up to 100 μ. Retuning requires an empty, idle store.

elements.label: Crystal Vial
elements.alt: The first persistent mana store, crafted from glass, copper, lapis, and a crystal shard.

elements.label: Raw Crystal Conduit
elements.alt: Four short-range raw conduits crafted from copper, glass, and crystal shards.

elements.label: Runed Mana Cell
elements.alt: Upgrade a Crystal Vial with runed conduits, gold, and a comparator.

elements.label: Resonant Vault
elements.alt: Upgrade a Runed Cell with resonant conduits, crying obsidian, amethyst, and diamond.

elements.label: Matched network tiers
elements.alt: Each storage tier accepts only its matching conduit tier; range, throughput, and efficiency rise together.

pages.title: Reading a Mana Quote
pages.body: The compiler quotes base, physical work, squared range, duration, rarity, memory, perception, and repeated control-flow work before execution. A Ponder fills each segment from the Program's real ManaCostModel breakdown.

elements.label: Eight-part cost prism
elements.alt: Eight labeled bands combine into the total pre-cast mana cost.

elements.label: Ponder the quote
elements.alt: Step through every non-authoritative display segment using the authoritative quote.

pages.title: Build and Compile
pages.body: Use the circle commands to create, place, parameterize, remove, undo, show, compile, and cast. Press V in a connected world for the server-backed graphical editor; press K for the latest Ponder. Ring 0 is outermost. Slot 0 is north. Exact diagnostics retain both this physical coordinate and the lowered instruction pointer.

elements.label: Editable typed starter
elements.alt: Run /vectorregnum circle vm_starter, then compile and inspect the highlighted order.

elements.label: Ponder compilation
elements.alt: A cursor visits every actual PlacedSigil in executionOrder.

elements.label: Bind the finished program
elements.alt: Open the spell media page.

pages.title: Faults and Wild Magic
pages.body: Compiler faults stop invalid bytecode from being published. Runtime faults are bounded and preserve their source. Compatibility spell failures may detonate internally, burst as an unstructured element, or become a violent miscast according to the actual CastResult.

elements.label: Fault path
elements.alt: Compilation fault stops before execution; runtime fault fractures the currently executing sigil; compatibility faults may emit Wild Magic.

elements.label: Ponder the real fault
elements.alt: Display the diagnostic, VM fault, or Wild Magic category carried by the actual result.

pages.title: Scroll, Book, and Tablet
pages.body: Bind a compiled circle into a scroll, spellbook, or carved tablet. A scroll burns only after its first accepted successful cast. A book is reusable. A tablet is permanent and casts from its verified world anchor.

elements.label: Three vessels, one spell
elements.alt: A scroll, reusable spellbook, and stone tablet each carry the same glowing circle in a different lifecycle.

elements.label: Blank scroll
elements.alt: Paper, ink, and amethyst make a single-use blank scroll.

elements.label: Blank spellbook
elements.alt: A book, lapis, and amethyst make a reusable spellbook.

elements.label: Carved tablet
elements.alt: Chiseled deepslate, lapis, and amethyst make a permanent anchored tablet.

elements.label: Ponder scroll consumption
elements.alt: The scroll remains through rejected casts and burns after the first accepted success.

pages.title: Movement Weaving
pages.body: Movement programs use typed points, vectors, entities, durations, and validated world effects. Vector Step and Kinetic Ward are the first live VM examples.

elements.label: Vector Step
elements.alt: A delayed impulse demonstrates a real WAITING tick followed by a validated world effect.
